title: The Magnet Bench
summary: Cut magnets in pieces, find the moment and poles of a solenoid, and match a bar magnet with a current.
subject: physics
concepts: Right-hand rule for the north pole
learningOutcome: The student can say what happens to the poles when a magnet is cut, find the magnetic moment of a solenoid and which end is north, and match a bar magnet with an equivalent solenoid.

levels.title: Cut the magnet
levels.adds: Baseline: cutting a magnet gives complete magnets, never a single isolated pole (Example 5.1).
hints: Each piece is a complete magnet with a north pole and a south pole.
The pieces point the same way as the original.
Isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist.

levels.title: A solenoid is a magnet
levels.adds: New idea: a solenoid has m = NIA, and the right-hand rule gives its north pole (Ex 5.3).
hints: m = N I A, with the area of one turn in m².
Curl the fingers of the right hand along the current in the windings.
The thumb points to the north pole.

levels.title: Match the magnet
levels.adds: More steps: choose the current so that a solenoid has the same magnetic moment as a bar magnet (Section 5.2).
hints: Equal magnets have equal magnetic moments.
Rearrange m = N I A for the current.
Convert the area from cm² to m².

misconceptions: Cutting a bar magnet separates the north and south poles
A solenoid has a magnetic moment only if it has an iron core
A thinner magnet cut along its length has a single pole
